rows: Nickel to golfball size hail fell from to McCamey to Rankin.
The public reported hail a little smaller than golfball size in Rankin.
Penny to quarter size hail was reported in and around McCamey, including at the intersection of U.S. Highway 67 and Texas Highway 349.

Local television meteorologists from all three networks in addition to severeal spotters reported a tornado on the ground north of Rankin. This tornado remained in open country and no damage was reported to the NWS.
Penny to quarter size hail fell in and around McCamey.
The Upton County Sheriff's Office reported 60 mph winds in McCamey. No damage was reported.
Penny to quarter size hail fell in McCamey.
A local television forecaster reported 80 mph winds in Rankin. No damage was reported.
Nickel size hail fell in 60-65 mph winds on the Midland/Upton County line.
A member of the media reported 60 to 65 mph winds along with nickel size hail along the Midland/Upton County line. No damage was reported.
Multiple reports of estimated wind speeds of 60 mph on Texas Highway 349. No damage was reported.
Law enforcement reported quarter sized hail on Texas State Highway 329.
A goat shelter in Rankin was damaged by strong thunderstorm winds.
Several trees were uprooted and one tree was snapped at the base of the trunk.
Severe winds broke one and a half inch diameter branches off of several trees and downed a thirty foot pine tree.

Several brief touchdowns were reported near Rankin, TX along US Highway 67. The tornado only lasted about two minutes and did not produce any damage along its short path. The path length and width of this tornado were estimated according to spotter reports.
High winds were also reported, although an estimate for the speed was not available.

A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced a brief tornado southwest of McCamey. A trained spotter reported that the tornado came down and went back up. No damage was reported with this tornado so it was rated as an EF-0.

A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced several brief tornado touchdowns near McCamey according to local law enforcement and fire department personnel. No damage was reported so these tornadoes are being rated as EF-0.
A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced tennis ball sized hail northeast of Rankin. There was a report of a broken car windshield. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced thunderstorm wind damage northeast of McCamey. Powerlines were blown down on Ranch to Market Road 2463 between US 67 and TX 329. Eight power poles were snapped along this stretch of road. The cost of damage is a very rough est…

Trained spotters viewed and took images of a tornado that developed two miles east of the community of Midkiff along Farm to Market Road 2401 and continued northeastward into open fields in extreme southwest portions of Glasscock County. The tornado was narrow, perhaps 50 to 75 y…

A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced wind damage in Rankin. There was a trampoline blown into the power lines, and a portable building was blown over behind the Rankin Drive In. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced a tornado six miles southeast of Rankin. The tornado was confirmed in open country south of Highway 67. There was no damage reported with this tornado so it was rated as an EF-0.
A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced a 59 mph wind gust near McCamey.

A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced a tornado near McCamey. The tornado touched down four miles north of McCamey for a couple of seconds in an open field then lifted. It was classified as an EF-0.
A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced a 69 mph wind gust in McCamey.
A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced a 68 mph wind gust near McCamey at the mesonet site.
A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced golfball sized hail. A windshield was broken on a patrol vehicle. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Mesonet Station 1SSW McCamey reported a 65 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
This report was received from mPING.

This report was received from mPING.
This report was received from mPING.
A trained spotter reported quarter to ping pong ball size hail, a half a mile to three miles south of McCamey.
Law enforcement reported nickel to quarter size hail in McCamey.
Quarter to half dollar size hail was reported at the Sheriff's office in Rankin.
A report of 3 inch diameter hail was reported from 8 miles east of Rankin.
Ping pong to golf ball-sized hail reported by the public via social media. Time was estimated by radar.
A report of penny sized hail was received from mPING. Time is estimated from radar.
A report of a 75 mph wind gust was received from an observer in McCamey with a personal anemometer. The time of occurrence is partially estimated.
